newsitem.title: FRANCE: Quick sale undervalues Aerospatiale - union.
newsitem.headline: Quick sale undervalues Aerospatiale - union.

text.p: The French government's decision to speed up privatisation of Aerospatiale means the state is selling the aircraft maker at low prices, the Force Ouvriere (FO) labour union said on Wednesday.

"By accelerating the move and not observing the principle of waiting for two years of profitability before any privatisation...the government undervalues the company, as the privatisation will come at the worst possible time," the union said in a statement.
The defence ministry earlier said Aerospatiale would be sold after merging with Dassault Aviation in the spring.
The FO said it wanted a meeting as quickly as possible with Prime Minister Alain Juppe to discuss its concerns over Aerospatiale.
Aerospatiale is being prepared for privatisation while it is in negotiations for a change in status of Airbus Industrie, the union said.

This raised fears among the employees that Aerospatiale was being carved up and would not have the financial strength to carry out the merger with Dassault, set up the new Airbus company, or consider the purchase with Alcatel Alsthom of Thomson-CSF, it said.
French newspapers have reported that the merged Aerospatiale/Dassault group could launch a joint bid with Alcatel for defence electronics company Thomson-CSF, which is also being privatised.
Airbus is made up of Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
